# TSE instruction set and register map

ISA version 1. A lane runs 16-bit instructions. Every instruction takes one cycle to dispatch, plus the delay, stall or slot wait listed for it, so a program's timing is exact to the cycle; the compiler and the assembler's timing API use the same numbers. This page is generated from `isa/tse_isa.yaml` and `isa/tse_regs.yaml`, which also generate the SystemVerilog packages and the assembler tables.

## Machine model

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Instruction word | 16 bits; op in bits [15:13], side-set value in [12:11] |
| Program memory | each lane reads a window of 128 SRAM words (two instructions per word, 256 instructions, 8-bit PC) |
| Fetch slots | lane k owns the SRAM in cycles with cycle mod 4 == k |
| Fetch buffer | 2 words per lane, least recently used replaced; fetch latency 1 |
| Data slots | lane k owns data-window cycles with cycle mod 16 == 4k + 3 |
| Registers | X, Y (16 bits), T (timeout counter), ISR and OSR (32-bit shift registers), clock C, PC |

Pipeline latencies (measured at the pins by `test/rtl/tb_chip_pins.sv`):

| Constant | Cycles | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `instr_to_port` | 2 | an instruction dispatched in cycle c changes the output port at edge c + n |
| `port_to_wait` | 2 | an input change during cycle k is seen by WAIT in cycle k + n |
| `emit_to_trig_port` | 3 | EMIT in cycle c changes the trigger-out port at edge c + n |
| `cfg_write_visible` | 2 | CSRW to a configuration word in cycle c is used by the assists from c + n |
| `edge_to_port` | 1 | pin-edge response rule: an edge seen in cycle e changes the port at edge e + tick_delay + n |

## Instructions

| Mnemonic | Match | Cycles | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `JMP` | op=0 | 1 cycle | Jump to target if cond holds. XDEC and YDEC test for nonzero, then decrement. |
| `WAIT` | op=1 | 1 cycle, plus `delay` delay cycles, plus the stall until the condition holds | Stall until the signal equals pol (or the alternate holds, or T expires), then delay cycles. |
| `SET` | op=2 | 1 cycle | Write an immediate. PINS and PINDIRS use imm[7:4] as a write mask for imm[3:0]. |
| `MOV` | op=3 | 1 cycle, plus `delay` delay cycles | Copy a 16-bit register. dst PC is a computed jump. |
| `OUT` | op=4 | 1 cycle, plus `delay` delay cycles | Shift n bits (1 to 32) out of OSR, LSB first, into dst. |
| `IN` | op=5 | 1 cycle, plus `delay` delay cycles | Shift n bits (1 to 32) from src into ISR, MSB first. |
| `PUSH` | op=6, sub=0 | 1 cycle, plus a stall when `blk` is set | ISR to the host RX mailbox, then clear ISR. blk stalls while the mailbox is full. |
| `PULL` | op=6, sub=1 | 1 cycle, plus a stall when `blk` is set | Host TX mailbox to OSR. Non-blocking PULL on an empty mailbox copies X instead. |
| `CSRW` | op=6, sub=2 | 1 cycle, plus 2 when the register is a configuration word (class L) | Write {Y,X} to lane register addr. Configuration words (class L) take 3 cycles in total. |
| `STW` | op=6, sub=2, dw=1 | 1 cycle, retires at dispatch; the next instruction waits for the lane's data slot s and runs at s + 1 | Store ISR to data window word addr in the lane's next data slot. |
| `CSRR` | op=6, sub=3 | 1 cycle | Read lane register addr into {Y,X}. |
| `LDW` | op=6, sub=3, dw=1 | 1 cycle, retires at dispatch; the next instruction waits for the lane's data slot s and runs at s + 2 | Load data window word addr into OSR in the lane's next data slot. |
| `DLY` | op=7, sub=0 | 1 cycle, plus `d` delay cycles | Do nothing for 1 + d cycles. |
| `TMR` | op=7, sub=1 | 1 cycle, plus `delay` delay cycles | Timed-automaton clock control. |
| `SIG` | op=7, sub=2 | 1 cycle | Write chip flags CF[3:0] under mask (visible to every lane next cycle). |
| `EMIT` | op=7, sub=3 | 1 cycle, plus `delay` delay cycles | Send event (code, X[7:0]) to the event unit. Never stalls. |

### Encodings

Every instruction also carries `op` in bits [15:13] and the side-set value in bits [12:11]. Bits not listed are reserved and must be 0; the decoder halts the lane on a reserved encoding.

**JMP** (op=0)

| Bits | Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [10:8] | `cond` | ALWAYS=0, XZ=1, XDEC=2, YDEC=3, XNEY=4, PIN=5, TOUT=6, GUARD=7 |
| [7:0] | `target` | jump target (label) |

**WAIT** (op=1)

| Bits | Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [10] | `pol` |  |
| [9:8] | `src` | PIN=0, EV=1, FLAG=2, CHIP=3 |
| [7:5] | `idx` | event name, by `src` (see the event table) |
| [4] | `to` | keyword `to`; time out when T counts down to 0 |
| [3] | `alt` | keyword `alt`; also end on the lane's alternate condition (LANE_CFG.alt_*) |
| [2:0] | `delay` |  |

**SET** (op=2)

| Bits | Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [10:8] | `dst` | PINS=0, PINDIRS=1, X=2, Y=3, T=4, XH=5, IRQ=6, CMD=7 |
| [7:0] | `imm` |  |

**MOV** (op=3)

| Bits | Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [10:8] | `dst` | X=0, Y=1, PINS=2, PINDIRS=3, ISR=4, OSR=5, T=6, PC=7 |
| [7:5] | `src` | X=0, Y=1, PINS=2, ISR=3, OSR=4, T=5, NOTX=6, C=7 |
| [4:0] | `delay` |  |

**OUT** (op=4)

| Bits | Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [10:8] | `dst` | PINS=0, PINDIRS=1, X=2, Y=3, NULL=4, T=5 |
| [7:3] | `n` | encoded as the written value minus 1 |
| [2:0] | `delay` |  |

**IN** (op=5)

| Bits | Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [10:8] | `src` | PINS=0, X=1, Y=2, ZEROS=3, ONES=4, OSR=5 |
| [7:3] | `n` | encoded as the written value minus 1 |
| [2:0] | `delay` |  |

**PUSH** (op=6, sub=0)

| Bits | Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [10:9] | `sub` |  |
| [8] | `blk` | keyword `block` |

**PULL** (op=6, sub=1)

| Bits | Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [10:9] | `sub` |  |
| [8] | `blk` | keyword `block` |

**CSRW** (op=6, sub=2)

| Bits | Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [10:9] | `sub` |  |
| [7:0] | `addr` | lane register address (see the lane registers) |

**STW** (op=6, sub=2, dw=1)

| Bits | Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [10:9] | `sub` |  |
| [8] | `dw` |  |
| [7] | `ind` | operand `X`; 1: word address from X[6:0] (addr must then be 0) |
| [6:0] | `addr` |  |
| | | constraint: if {'ind': 1} then {'addr': 0} |

**CSRR** (op=6, sub=3)

| Bits | Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [10:9] | `sub` |  |
| [7:0] | `addr` | lane register address (see the lane registers) |

| Bits | Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [10:9] | `sub` |  |
| [8] | `dw` |  |
| [7] | `ind` | operand `X`; 1: word address from X[6:0] (addr must then be 0) |
| [6:0] | `addr` |  |
| | | constraint: if {'ind': 1} then {'addr': 0} |

**DLY** (op=7, sub=0)

| Bits | Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [10:9] | `sub` |  |
| [8:0] | `d` |  |

**TMR** (op=7, sub=1)

| Bits | Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [10:9] | `sub` |  |
| [8] | `cclr` | keyword `cclr`; reset clock C to 0 |
| [7] | `gwe` | set when `gsel=` is given; write gsel |
| [6:5] | `gsel` | written `gsel=n`; guard threshold GT[gsel] compared with C |
| [4:0] | `delay` |  |

| Bits | Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|

### Operand names

| Enumeration | Values |
|---|---|
| `cond` | ALWAYS=0, XZ=1, XDEC=2, YDEC=3, XNEY=4, PIN=5, TOUT=6, GUARD=7 |
| `wsrc` | PIN=0, EV=1, FLAG=2, CHIP=3 |
| `setdst` | PINS=0, PINDIRS=1, X=2, Y=3, T=4, XH=5, IRQ=6, CMD=7 |
| `movdst` | X=0, Y=1, PINS=2, PINDIRS=3, ISR=4, OSR=5, T=6, PC=7 |
| `movsrc` | X=0, Y=1, PINS=2, ISR=3, OSR=4, T=5, NOTX=6, C=7 |
| `outdst` | PINS=0, PINDIRS=1, X=2, Y=3, NULL=4, T=5 |
| `insrc` | PINS=0, X=1, Y=2, ZEROS=3, ONES=4, OSR=5 |

### WAIT and STATUS event indices

For `src` PIN, idx 0 to 3 are pin levels and 4 to 7 mean "pin idx - 4 changed since the WAIT dispatched".

| Source | Names |
|---|---|
| `EV` | TXNEED=0, TIMER=0, RXFULL=1, RULEHIT=2, CRCOK=3, ERR=4, BITSTART=5, TXIDLE=6, ABORT=7 |
| `FLAG` | GUARD=0, SAMPLE=1, HALF=2, EDGE=3, HTXF=4, HRXE=5, SYNCED=6, ONE=7 |
| `CHIP` | CF0=0, CF1=1, CF2=2, CF3=3, TRIG=4, TICK=5 |

## Register map

Classes: **L** configuration word (latch, cleared by the loader, not by reset; a lane's CSRW takes 3 cycles; programs cannot read it), **F** runtime flop (reset by rst_n), **P** write-only command pulse, **R** read-only.

### Host address regions

| Region | Base | Size | Contents |
|---|---|---|---|
| sram | 0x0000 | 0x0200 | program SRAM words; window w at 0x80 x w; window 3 is the data window |
| data | 0x0400 | 0x0080 | data window for LDW and STW (alias of SRAM window 3) |
| fallback | 0x0800 | 0x0008 | fallback latch program store |
| lanes | 0x1000 | 0x0200 | lane registers at 0x1000 + 0x100 x lane + reg |
| xbar | 0x2000 | 0x0040 | crossbar |
| event | 0x3000 | 0x0040 | event unit |
| chip | 0x4000 | 0x0040 | chip control, status and mailboxes |

### Lane registers (CSRW and CSRR address; host address 0x1000 + 0x100 x lane + address)

| Address | Name | Class | Fields | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x00 | `CRC_POLY` | L | poly[31:0] | polynomial, left-aligned |
| 0x01 | `CRC_INIT` | L | init[31:0] | initial value, left-aligned |
| 0x02 | `CRC_XOR` | L | xorout[31:0] | final XOR in transmission order, left-aligned |
| 0x03 | `CRC_CHECK` | L | check[31:0] | expected residue, left-aligned |
| 0x04 | `CRC_CTL` | L | wm1[4:0], refin[5], refout[6] | width minus 1 and reflection |
| 0x08 | `STUFF_CFG` | L | n[3:0], ones[4], zeros[5] | stuff after n equal bits (0 off) |
| 0x09 | `CODEC_CFG` | L | mode[1:0] (NRZ=0, NRZI=1, MANCHESTER=2), inv[2], t_on1[3] | line code |
| 0x10 | `DPLL_PERIOD` | L | period[19:0] | bit period in 1/16 cycle |
| 0x11 | `DPLL_SPT` | L | spt[19:0] | sample point from bit start in 1/16 cycle |
| 0x12 | `DPLL_SJW` | L | sjw[15:0] | largest correction per resync in 1/16 cycle |
| 0x13 | `DPLL_CTL` | L | resync[0], dual[1], rise[2], fall[3] | resync and edge options |
| 0x14 | `TIMER_INC` | L | inc[23:0] | NCO increment: tick rate = f_clk x inc / 2^24 |
| 0x15 | `TIMER_CTL` | L | reload[15:0], on_tick[16], en[17], ev0_sel[18] | lane timer reload, mode and event 0 select |
| 0x18 | `LANE_CFG` | L | txpin[1:0], rxpin[3:2], ss_base[5:4], side_en[6], jmp_pin[8:7], tx_msb[9], rx_msb[10], tx_crc[11], rx_crc[12], arb_en[13], resp_coded[14], tx_owns_pin[15], rx_len_m1[20:16], idle[21], alt_pol[22], alt_src[24:23] (PIN=0, EV=1, FLAG=2, CHIP=3), alt_idx[27:25] | pins, framing, options and the WAIT alternate condition |
| 0x19 | `LANE_PROG` | L | start_pc[7:0], window[9:8], fallback[10] | start address, SRAM window, fallback store |
| 0x1a | `GUARD01` | L | gt0[15:0], gt1[31:16] | guard thresholds GT0 and GT1 in cycles |
| 0x1b | `GUARD23` | L | gt2[15:0], gt3[31:16] | guard thresholds GT2 and GT3 in cycles |
| 0x20 | `TXDATA` | F | data[31:0] | word to send; the write starts transmission |
| 0x21 | `TXCTL` | F | count_m1[4:0], append_crc[5] | bits to send minus 1, CRC append |
| 0x22 | `RXDATA` | R | data[31:0] | last complete RX word; reading clears RXFULL |
| 0x23 | `STATUS` | R | ev[7:0], tflag[8], illegal[9], running[10], hits[12:11], rx_count[17:13], tx_active[18], crc_busy[19], serr[20], abort[21], aflag[22], timer[23], pc[31:24] | lane status |
| 0x24 | `CMD` | P | frame_rst[0], crc_clear[1], hard_arm[2], tx_abort[3], dpll_on[4], dpll_off[5], line_set[6], line_val[7] | command pulses (also SET CMD) |
| 0x25 | `CRC_RESULT` | R | result[31:0] | CRC register XOR CRC_XOR, left-aligned (reflected, so right-aligned, with refout) |
| 0x26 | `CLOCK` | R | c[15:0] | current value of the clock C |
| 0x28 | `TS` | R | ts[31:0] | chip timestamp (alias of the event unit TS) |
| 0x40 | `RULE0_MATCH` | L | pattern[15:0], mask[31:16] | rule 0 pattern and compare mask |
| 0x41 | `RULE0_RESP_POS` | L | resp[15:0], pos[23:16], any[24] | rule 0 response bits and frame bit position |
| 0x42 | `RULE0_CTL` | L | rlen_m1[3:0], offset[7:4], cond[9:8] (NONE=0, CRC_GOOD=1, CRC_BAD=2, TX_IDLE=3), drive[10], abort[11], en[12] | rule 0 control |
| 0x44 | `RULE1_MATCH` | L | pattern[15:0], mask[31:16] | rule 1 pattern and compare mask |
| 0x45 | `RULE1_RESP_POS` | L | resp[15:0], pos[23:16], any[24] | rule 1 response bits and frame bit position |
| 0x46 | `RULE1_CTL` | L | rlen_m1[3:0], offset[7:4], cond[9:8] (NONE=0, CRC_GOOD=1, CRC_BAD=2, TX_IDLE=3), drive[10], abort[11], en[12], chain[13] | rule 1 control (chain extends rule 0 to 32-bit patterns) |
| 0x48 | `RULE_CLK` | L | src[0], clk_pin[2:1], edge[3], tick_delay[11:4], hold[12] | what clocks both rules (bit mode or pin-edge mode); hold: a drive keeps its last bit until the program writes txpin |

| Address | Name | Class | Fields | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x2000 (x16) | `PAD_OUT` | L | src[3:0], inv[4], od[5], en[6], idle[7], idle_oe[8] | output pad p (0 to 7 uo_out, 8 to 15 uio) |
